summary.title: Why you shouldn't list certifications on LinkedIn
summary.one_liner: Interviewing.io's analysis of about 20K LinkedIn profiles and 40K anonymous interviews finds that listing certifications correlates with worse interview performance, with Triplebyte the only certifier showing a positive signal.
keywords: do online courses help get hired
takeaways: Candidates with LinkedIn certifications passed anonymous interviews about 53% of the time versus 57% for those without (p < 0.00001).
The gap persists after controlling for interview language/focus and shrinks by about 40% after controlling for pedigree, but is not fully explained.
Among the top 10 certifiers, Triplebyte was the only one associated with a positive effect (+6 percentage points); Cisco was the worst (-10 points).
The author argues certifications create a feedback loop where recruiters learn to distrust them, harming non-traditional candidates the most.
summary.summary: Aline Lerner of interviewing.io argues that certifications on LinkedIn are a negative signal for hiring, and tests this with data from over 100k technical interviews on the platform. The author aggregated interview scores for about 20K LinkedIn profiles, 28% of which listed a certification, and ran regressions across roughly 40k interview observations. The analysis controls for interview language and focus and for candidate pedigree, and then breaks out the top 10 certification issuers. The post is self-described as correlational, since platform interview performance is only a proxy for real engineering ability.
